summary: Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was an Indologist. In 1884, he served as Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College, subsequently becoming Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College (circa 1884–1914) and permanent Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai.

Shridhar Tryambak Pathak was an Indologist. He held posts as a Shastri at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1921) and as a Sanskrit Teacher at Elphinstone College (attested 1927).

Shrikant S. Bahulkar works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale, served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held positions at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth and Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Shrinarayan Mishra was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who studied under Anantalal Thakur. His career was centered at Banaras Hindu University, where he served as Lecturer in Sanskrit (attested 1971), Reader (attested 1985), and Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit (attested 2010).

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1914–1937) and served the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute as Secretary (~1918–1927) and Mahabharata General Editor (1948–1961).

Shrivatsa Goswami is an Indologist and religious studies philosopher who studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University (~1968–1974), where he also taught. He was a visiting scholar at Harvard University (~1976–1977) and affiliated with Vrindaban Research Institute.

Shu-chen Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia, where she worked as a teaching assistant in 1996 and was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen Christina Lang.

Shu-fen Chen is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She studied at National Tsing Hua University, completed her doctorate under Hans Henrich Hock, and became a professor at National Tsing Hua University.

Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar. His career includes appointments as a Professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and in the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

Shudo Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shigeo Kamata and earned his BA and doctorate at Komazawa University. He spent his academic career at Komazawa University, serving as assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor.

Shuhong Chang was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied in China and France. He taught at the Central Academy of Fine Arts and National Academy of Art, later serving as director of the Dunhuang Academy.

Shuichi Kato was a scholar of Japanology, history, and philosophy who earned a medical degree at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the University of British Columbia, Sophia University, and directed the Kyoto Museum for World Peace.
Shuichi Maida was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and was a student of Haya Akegarasu.

Shuichi Nara specializes in Indology and philosophy. He was educated at Keio University and serves as a full-time researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute as well as a lecturer at Chuo University.

Shuji Takayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has held positions as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University, commissioned researcher at Bukkyo University, visiting researcher at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, and researcher at Musashino University.

Shujiro Shimada was a scholar of Japanology, sinology, and history/archaeology. He was educated at Kyoto University from circa 1928 to 1931 and held a post at Princeton University from circa 1962 to 1975.

Shujun Motegi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and earned an MA from Kyoto University, later serving as a Professor of Ethics at Shinshu University.

Shuken Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at Komazawa University. He spent his career at Komazawa University as an assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor, and was a visiting professor at Aichi Gakuin University.

Shuman Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen studied under the traditional teacher Weijue Shi and completed a PhD at Northwestern University under the supervision of Brook Ziporyn.

Shuming Liang was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies who attended Shuntian Middle School. In 1917, he held a post in the philosophy department at Peking University, and he later founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute.
